# Ferrum: Stud Finder & Metal

> Ferrum is an iPhone app (iOS 17 or later) by 55DIGITS LLC that uses the phone's magnetometer to find ferrous metal behind walls: the screws or nails that hold a wooden stud, steel framing and pipes, live wiring that is carrying current, and lost iron or steel objects. $4.99 once on the US App Store; no subscription, no in-app purchases, no ads. No data collected; works offline.

- Does: four modes — Stud, Wire (50/60 Hz current that is flowing), Metal, Recovery (Max Hold).
- Does not: detect gold, silver, copper, aluminum, brass or plastic; measure depth; see a cable with no current; see wood itself.
- Page: https://ferrumstudfinder.com/
- App Store: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/id6802032570
- Contact: ferrum@tommano.com

## Guides
- [Do stud finder apps really work on an iPhone?](https://ferrumstudfinder.com/guides/do-stud-finder-apps-work/): Stud finder apps work for one thing: finding the steel screws and nails in a stud with the iPhone's magnetometer. Here is what they can and cannot detect, with our own test numbers.
- [How to find a stud without a stud finder](https://ferrumstudfinder.com/guides/find-a-stud-without-a-stud-finder/): Six ways to find a wall stud without a stud finder: outlets and switches, measuring from a corner, trim nails, the knock test, a magnet, and your phone's magnetometer.
- [Best stud finder app, or a real stud finder? How to choose](https://ferrumstudfinder.com/guides/stud-finder-app-vs-stud-finder/): What makes a stud finder app good, and when a real stud finder is the better buy. A phone app, a magnetic finder, an electronic finder and a wall scanner each detect different things.
- [How to find wires in a wall before you drill](https://ferrumstudfinder.com/guides/find-live-wires-in-a-wall/): Where cables usually run, which tools detect them, and what an iPhone can and cannot tell you about live wiring behind a wall. A phone senses flowing current, not the wire itself.
